retirement:earlyend: Own-terms end on the stated 'until' date. Under the owner's 2026-10-21 ruling the end is recorded as that date, inclusive (the exemption runs through the end of that day); the exclusive reading, under which the exemption stops when that day begins, is the stated alternative. The employee's death or separation before the date would leave the exemption unused but is not, on the order's text, an end of the order, and no held record shows such an event. The date is a fixed term of the grant, not a deadline on some other act.
retirement:indep: The order contains one operative command, the time-limited exemption of one named employee. The recital of section 204 and the identification of the employee are not independent commands.
retirement:savings: Service performed and pay earned while the exemption ran are accrued effects. Any annuity or retirement-credit consequence flows from the retirement statutes, not from the order, and does not keep the order operative: the order commands nothing after its stated date and no later order names it.
retirement:search: Searches made on 2026-10-28: (1) census titles in jobs/domesday-register/output/REGISTER.csv and type rows in jobs/x1-class-engine/output/TYPES.csv for the person's surname; (2) every entry of the WPA 1944 numbered list (jobs/x1-class-engine/data/WPA_NUMBERED_ENTRIES.csv, whitespace-insensitive) for the surname; (3) a full-text search of every held order text under jobs/*/output/texts for the person's name; (4) the register list of every 'Compulsory Retirement' title dated after the order. The machine USC and eCFR citation searches (complete, 0 hits) exclude a current-law reference; the OFR catalog search starts in 1937 and is not adequate alone.
retirement:statute: Authority: section 204 of Part II of the Legislative Appropriation Act of June 30, 1932 (47 Stat. 382, 404), whose proviso lets the President exempt a person from automatic separation at retirement age. No held source shows section 204 repealed or amended before this order's stated end. Held texts of later exemptions show the President still granting exemptions under section 204 after this date (for example EO 7725 of October 1937, under section 204, running to November 1, 1938), which corroborates that the statutory scheme ran through the stated date.
